message.content: In lions, one of the most striking examples of a dominant genetic trait is the presence and size of the mane in adult males. The gene(s) responsible for mane development are expressed dominantly, meaning that a single copy of the allele (inherited from either parent) is sufficient to produce the trait. As a result, male lions typically develop a mane, while females do not because they lack the necessary hormonal trigger (testosterone) that activates the same genes. This dominant expression of mane-related genes is why mane presence is almost exclusively seen in male lions.
